description_full: Archrock, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates as an energy infrastructure company in the United States. The company operates in two segments, Contract Operations and Aftermarket Services. It engages in the designing, sourcing, owning, installing, operating, servicing, repairing, and maintaining of its owned fleet of natural gas compression equipment to provide natural gas compression services. The company also sells over-the-counter parts and components, as well as provides operations, major and routine maintenance, overhaul, and reconfiguration services to customers who own compression equipment. It serves integrated and independent oil and natural gas processors, gatherers, and transporters. Archrock, Inc. was formerly known as Exterran Holdings, Inc. and changed its name to Archrock, Inc. in November 2015. The company was founded in 1990 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.

financial_summary: Archrock, Inc. is a mid-cap energy business with a $4.8B market cap on $1.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +21% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 46%.

The business throws off $120M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.93× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.8× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.6×.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.7% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 3.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
